title: Astro-Mine-Bench — submission pipeline
description: The submit -> evaluate -> score -> rank pipeline (bench.md §10). Queue depth, the re-execution mismatch rate (the key integrity signal), evaluation latency, and the authorization / supply-chain / sandbox signals from bench#29 and bench#30. Scraped from the leaderboard's /metrics endpoint (astro_mine.bench.telemetry).

panels.title: Queue depth
panels.description: Submissions accepted and awaiting an evaluation worker. The primary back-pressure signal for the evaluation fleet (bench.md §8, §10). A depth that climbs without draining means the fleet is undersized or a worker is wedged.

panels.title: Re-execution mismatch rate — THE INTEGRITY SIGNAL
panels.description: The fraction of sampled provenance re-executions that did NOT reproduce their recorded result. bench.md §10 calls this 'a key integrity signal': a non-zero, sustained rate means submissions are non-deterministic or being tampered with, and the leaderboard's central anti-gaming claim (bench.md §9) is failing. It should sit flat at zero. Any sustained rise is a page, not a ticket.

panels.title: Evaluation latency (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Wall-clock of each pipeline stage, from the astro_mine_bench_evaluation_duration_seconds histogram. bench.md §8's hosted SLO: a standard-budget evaluation (~50 seeds of the anchor scenario) completes in minutes-to-low-hours. The `stage` label separates evaluate from reexecute.

panels.title: Evaluation throughput
panels.description: Submissions reaching a terminal state per second, by outcome (bench.md §10). The _count rate of the evaluation histogram is the fleet's real throughput.

panels.title: Supply-chain verification failures (bench#29)
panels.description: Hub submissions rejected because their cosign signature, SLSA provenance, or SBOM did not verify. A sustained rise means either a broken publisher toolchain or someone pushing unsigned artifacts at the leaderboard.

panels.title: Authorization denials + sandbox terminations (bench#29 / bench#30)
panels.description: Left: authorization decisions by action and outcome — a spike in denials is an attack indicator or a misconfigured IdP. Right: how often a submission is killed by its sandbox envelope (timeout / memory / crash), which is both an abuse signal and a sign the envelope may be too tight for legitimate work.
